name: Yellow-bellied Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Humid lowlands of southern mexico (oaxaca) to northeastern costa rica
description: A tiny, stub-tailed flycatcher of humid tropical forest. Spends most of its time in the canopy, where overlooked easily, but at times descends lower, mainly at forest edges.

name: Black-backed Tanager
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southeastern brazil (rio de janeiro to santa catarina)
description: Beautiful multicolored tanager found in coastal forests, forest edges, and gardens where it forages in pairs or small groups. Males are blue-green below with a cinnamon head, black mask, black back, and straw-colored rump, vent, and wing coverts.

name: Sumatran Drongo
rangeDescription: Humid lowlands of sumatra
description: Glossy large-billed drongo with glossy blue-sheened wings and tail. Also note bright red eyes, iridescent speckling around the throat and neck, and flared broad-tipped tail.

name: Yellow-headed Manakin
rangeDescription: Western and central andes of colombia and northeastern ecuador
description: Rare and local in cloud forest from around 1,200-2,400m. Unique: mostly olive with contrasting yellow crown and dull reddish eye.

name: Gray-backed Storm-Petrel
rangeDescription: Circumpolar subantarctic waters, north to about 35°s
description: A very small seabird of southern oceans. Gray-black on head, neck, throat, and top of breast.

name: Lesser Spotted Eagle
rangeDescription: Locally in eastern europe to caspian lowlands; winters to southern africa
description: Medium-sized, compact eagle. Adults are conspicuously two toned when perched: dark flight feathers contrast with paler body.

name: Gray Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Mulga woodland of inland western australia
description: Small plain desert honeyeater of inland Western and central Australia that is seldom observed. Relatively short, decurved bill and extremely plain plumage, gray above, paler gray below, with no obvious field marks other than faint pale tips to some tail feathers.
imageCreditName: Laurie Ross | Tracks Birding & Photography Tours

name: Sao Tome Grosbeak
rangeDescription: São tomé (gulf of guinea)
description: A large uniform chestnut finch with a robust pink-horn bill. Endemic to São Tomé and very rare; once thought to be extinct.

name: Red-necked Amazon
rangeDescription: Montane forest of dominica (lesser antilles)
description: A chunky and gregarious resident of wet upland forests; often found in flocks of up to 15 birds. Its green body, bluish head, and orange-red spot on upper chest readily separates this species from the Imperial Parrot, the only other parrot sharing its range, as well as parrot species commonly kept in captivity.

name: El Oro Parakeet
rangeDescription: Andean foothills of southwestern ecuador (el oro and azuay)
description: Rare and endangered parakeet endemic to foothill cloud forest in southwestern Ecuador. It is mostly green with red on forehead, shoulder, and undertail.

name: Black-backed Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Boreal forest of northern north america
description: Dark woodpecker, inconspicuous and uncommon. Found in coniferous forests, often in recently burned areas or bogs with many dead trees.

name: Ward's Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Rainforest of eastern madagascar
description: Small black-and-white vanga that looks uncannily like a monarch flycatcher. Madagascar endemic that is found in the canopy of eastern rainforest at middle elevations.

name: Black-capped Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Mountains of costa rica and western panama
description: Small flycatcher, darker than other similar species, with particularly noteworthy black cap and teardrop-shaped white eyering. Dull brownish wingbars.

name: Sapphire-bellied Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Coastal north-central colombia
description: Rare, endangered, and poorly known hummingbird restricted to mangroves and adjacent scrubby areas along the Colombian coast. Male has sapphire underparts extending from throat all the way to belly, and lacks the distinct hood typical of the more common Sapphire-throated Hummingbird.

name: Buru Flowerpecker
rangeDescription: Buru island (southern moluccas)
description: A tiny, stub-tailed gray songbird. Has an entirely gray upperside, a bright white throat, and whitish underparts with extensively gray-washed flanks and a white tuft of feathers on the shoulder.

name: Roll's Partridge
rangeDescription: Northwestern sumatra (batak highlands)
description: Restricted to montane and foothill broadleaf forests between 500 and 2000 meters in the Batak Highlands of northern Sumatra. Forages in dense vegetation on the forest floor, often pairs, but also singly and in small groups.

name: Chestnut Bunting
rangeDescription: Siberia to northern mongolia and northeastern china; winters to india and southeastern asia
description: Small, shy bunting, usually seen through a screen of thick shrubby vegetation in low, dense thickets. Brightly colored adult male distinctive, with brilliant chestnut upperparts and a daisy-yellow belly.

name: Cape Starling
rangeDescription: Acacia of western gabon and angola to south africa
description: A medium-sized iridescent blue-green glossy starling that lacks dark ear-patches and has greenish flanks and belly, giving it a more uniform appearance than the “blue-eared” starlings. Pairs and small groups occupy high-altitude grassland, Karoo, and savanna, including drier habitats than other glossy starlings.

name: Makira Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Makira (southeastern solomon islands)
description: A tiny warbler with a mostly gray head, a dark eye-stripe, and a pale eyebrow. Back and wings strongly green-toned with two buff wingbars.

name: Banggai Jungle Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Peleng, in banggai islands (off eastern sulawesi)
description: A drab flycatcher with brown upperparts, a paler gray underside, and rufous coloration in the tail, rump, and wing. Shows a pale mark between the bill and the eye.
